drafts.title: EU AI Act Article 50 hits August 2, 2026 — most content creators have no idea their AI-generated posts are already a compliance liability
drafts.text:
Been going deep on the EU AI Act's Article 50 (the one most compliance guides skip because it's not about high-risk AI).

Here's the thing: Article 50 isn't about how AI makes decisions — it's about labeling AI output. And it applies to basically everything: blog posts, AI images, voiceovers, ad copy, product descriptions.

Fine tier: same as GDPR's most serious violations. Up to €15M.

The catch: the labeling requirement is machine-readable, not just a visible text note. You need JSON-LD schema in your HTML, C2PA manifests in images, XMP metadata in audio files. Not a disclaimer in your footer.

I built a free tool that generates the correct disclosure label (HTML badge + JSON-LD + C2PA template) for any content type in about 60 seconds. Deadline is 71 days out. Full breakdown:
https://tinytools-smoky.vercel.app/ai-disclosure-generator/blog/your-ai-content-is-missing-a-required-label-eu-ai-act-deadline-2026/

drafts.title: I timed 3 recruiters reviewing GitHub profiles. Average decision: 8 seconds. Here's what killed each one.
drafts.text:
Did an informal experiment: got 3 senior engineering recruiters to review 12 anonymized GitHub profiles while I recorded their commentary and timed their first impression.

Results were brutal. 6 of 12 profiles got a skip before the recruiter scrolled at all. The main culprits:

1. Tutorial repo graveyards pinned at the top (todo-app, weather-app, etc.)
2. Commit graphs that flatline for months then spike right before job search season
3. Empty or placeholder READMEs
4. Bio that says 'aspiring' or 'learning to code' above entry level
5. Zero stars/forks signaling no one else has engaged with your work

Full breakdown with direct recruiter quotes + free AI roast tool that catches these in 30 seconds:
https://tinytools-smoky.vercel.app/github-roast/blog/your-github-profile-is-getting-you-ghosted-recruiters-2026/
